{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "ULTRA WEBSITE PROMPT – CYBERTRAVEL LOG / STATIC PRODUCT SHOWCASE BLOG

Create a premium static website in React + Tailwind for a futuristic travel blog/product showcase called “Neon Nomad Notes”. It should feel like Notion meets cyberpunk travel magazine: clean modular content blocks, editorial cards, soft documentation-style layout, but with neon gradients, dark glass panels, glowing borders, and cursor-reactive effects.

IMPORTANT: This is a pure static front-end only. No backend, no login, no database, no real API, no external live data. Use mock/static sample content directly in the code. Everything must work as a static site.

BRAND STYLE
- Name: Neon Nomad Notes
- Domain/theme: travel blog + curated travel gear/product showcase
- Visual vibe: cyberpunk, night city, digital passport, neon airports, future hotels, rainy streets, terminal boards
- Reference feeling: Notion-style structured pages, clean blocks, sidebar notes, databases/cards, tags, minimal content hierarchy
- Colors:
  - Background: near black #070812 / deep navy #0B1020
  - Primary neon: electric cyan #00F5FF
  - Secondary neon: magenta #FF2BD6
  - Accent: acid green #B6FF00
  - Text: white / slate / muted gray
- Use Tailwind CSS heavily
- Use modern responsive layout
- No heavy animations that break performance
- Medium complexity, polished enough for a landing page + blog showcase

MAIN GOAL
Build a static product-showcase travel blog landing page that presents:
1. Featured futuristic travel articles
2. Curated travel gear cards
3. Destination guide cards
4. A Notion-inspired travel dashboard section
5. CTA for reading the guide / exploring kit / downloading static checklist

PAGE STRUCTURE

1) TOP NAVIGATION
- Sticky transparent/glass nav
- Left: logo icon simple text “Neon Nomad Notes”
- Nav links: Home, Field Notes, Gear Vault, Routes, Checklist
- Right side: small pill button “Start Exploring”
- Add small neon status text: “Static dispatch • 2026 edition”
- Mobile responsive hamburger is fine, but can be simple static menu if easier

2) HERO SECTION
Create a strong hero area:
- Small badge: “Cyberpunk Travel Blog • Static Guide”
- Huge headline: “Travel the future without losing your signal.”
- Subheadline: “A curated log of neon cities, compact travel gear, airport survival notes, and visual route boards for digital nomads.”
- CTA buttons:
  - “Read Latest Notes”
  - “View Gear Kit”
- Hero visual on right: Notion-like dashboard mockup card with nested blocks:
  - Trip: Tokyo Night Loop
  - Budget: ¥ Static estimate
  - Weather: mock text only
  - Gear score: 92/100
  - Tags: neon food, capsule hotel, rail pass, night market
- Add floating cards around hero:
  - “Next route: Seoul → Taipei”
  - “Carry-on kit: 18 items”
  - “Signal safe zones mapped”
- Use gradients and subtle glow.

3) CURSOR EFFECTS REQUIREMENT
Add front-end cursor effects, but keep it static and simple:
- Custom glowing cursor dot / ring on desktop
- Cards should slightly glow or tilt/raise on hover
- Maybe neon trail gradient following mouse via CSS/React state is okay
- Do NOT use canvas, WebGL, physics, or game-like mechanics
- If reduced motion is preferred, keep it elegant and not distracting

4) FEATURED FIELD NOTES SECTION
Notion/blog style grid of articles. Use static mock content.
Title: “Latest Field Notes”
Cards should include category tag, title, excerpt, read time, location, and fake date.
Create at least 6 article cards:
- “Tokyo After Midnight: 7 Stops on the Yamanote Glow Loop”
- “How to Pack for 72 Hours in a Rainy Megacity”
- “Capsule Hotels, Quiet Floors, and Sleep Pods Reviewed”
- “The Neon Food Hall Index: Seoul Edition”
- “Airport Layover Survival Map: Singapore Terminal Nights”
- “Digital Nomad Desk Setup in a 9m² Room”
Design cards like Notion database cards but cyberpunk: tags, icons, clean spacing, neon hover border.

5) PRODUCT SHOWCASE / GEAR VAULT
This is important: make it feel like a product showcase even though it’s a blog.
Section title: “Gear Vault: Static Carry-On Loadout”
Include 8 gear/product cards with mock products:
- SignalSafe Sling Bag
- NightRail Noise Filters
- CapsuleCharge 65W Brick
- HoloTag Luggage Card
- RainShell Urban Jacket
- Pocket Router Case
- FoldFlat Keyboard
- MicroTripod Vlog Stand
Each product card should show:
- product name
- category
- short description
- mock price
- rating stars or score
- small “why pack it” note
- button: “View notes” (non-functional or anchor only)
Design: dark cards, product placeholder gradient image/icon, neon accent stripe.
Do not integrate payments, cart, checkout, inventory, or real products. Static showcase only.

6) DESTINATION ROUTE BOARD
Create a section like an airport/train schedule but for travel routes.
Title: “Route Board”
Use table/list with cyberpunk terminal style:
Columns: Route, Mood, Duration, Best Time, Status
Rows:
- Tokyo → Osaka, Night rail, 3 days, April, Saved
- Seoul → Busan, Food loop, 2 days, October, Draft
- Taipei → Jiufen, Rainy hillside, 1 day, March, Ready
- Singapore → Kuala Lumpur, Urban contrast, 4 days, July, Saved
- Bangkok → Chiang Mai, Slow digital reset, 5 days, January, Draft
Static data only.

7) NOTION INSPIRED DASHBOARD SECTION
Create a large split section called “Trip OS Dashboard”
Left column: description about organizing travel notes like a second brain.
Right column: mock Notion-style interface with blocks:
- Today’s checklist
  - Charge power bank
  - Screenshot hotel address
  - Offline map saved
  - Pack rain layer
- Databases/cards:
  - Cities
  - Gear
  - Food stops
  - Transit notes
- Add progress bars for “Packing”, “Route Planning”, “Offline Prep”
Make it look clean, modular, and editorial.

8) FEATURED DESTINATION CARDS
Three big destination cards:
- Tokyo Neon Alleys
- Seoul Food Grid
- Taipei Rain Markets
Each card: big gradient image placeholder, location tag, 3 bullet highlights, CTA “Open guide”
Make them responsive and visually strong.

9) NEWSLETTER / STATIC CTA
Section title: “Download the Static Travel Checklist”
Text: “A mock downloadable checklist block for packing, route planning, and digital safety.”
Input field can be visual only; no real submit required. Button says “Preview Checklist”.
Mention small text: “No account, no tracking, no backend in this demo.”

10) FOOTER
Footer with columns:
- Neon Nomad Notes
- Explore: Field Notes, Gear Vault, Routes
- Resources: Packing List, City Cards, Desk Setup
- Tiny disclaimer: “Static concept site with sample content.”
Add social-style pills but no real links required.

DESIGN DETAILS
- Use Tailwind utility classes
- Responsive for mobile/tablet/desktop
- Use semantic sections
- Make typography premium: big headings, clear body, small uppercase labels
- Background should have subtle grid pattern, blurred neon blobs, maybe scanline overlay using CSS only
- Cards should use glassmorphism but remain readable
- Use icons from lucide-react if available, otherwise simple emoji/icons are fine
- Avoid generic boring travel stock look. Make it futuristic and editorial.

TECH REQUIREMENTS
- React + Tailwind preferred
- Static content arrays inside components are fine
- No fetching data
- No API keys
- No backend routes
- No database/auth/admin panel
- No 3D, no WebGL, no Three.js, no canvas animation
- Cursor effect should be CSS/React DOM only
- Deliver one polished page, can include multiple sections and anchor navigation

FINAL OUTPUT EXPECTATION
A complete static website landing page for a cyberpunk travel blog/product showcase, with Notion-like content organization, mock products, mock articles, responsive design, and tasteful cursor hover effects.",

 }

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
